svg.title: dsh-labor-contract structure: a three-tier local review bench, nine clause gates, three measurement scales, and a batch issue sheet that labor_export writes as a sha256-stamped CSV
svg.desc: Tier 01 clause bench: labor-contract.txt goes through labor_check (R0); each of the nine required clauses is tested twice, once for its keyword pattern and once for a concrete element, and lands on present, attention or missing; the quickstart fixture returns present 9, attention 0, missing 0. Tier 02 scales: the inclusive contract term in whole months picks the probation cap (under 3 months gives 0, 3 to 11 gives 1, 12 to 35 gives 2, 36 or more and open-ended give 6; fixture 36 months gives 6 against a 3-month probation), probation pay is compared in cents against the 80% floor (fixture 10800 of 12000 = 90.00%, so it passes), and the non-compete clause is measured against 24 months with a monthly-compensation prompt (fixture 24 months with compensation). Tier 03 issue sheet: employees.csv with seven columns and six rows goes through labor_batch (R0) with as_of 2026-11-02 and yields four issues, each shown as measured versus threshold; labor_export (R1) writes them as RFC 4180 CSV under $DSH_HOME/dsh-labor-contract/exports/labor-issues.csv, returning 4 rows, 566 bytes and a sha256 receipt. Everything is local: no network, no model call, not legal advice.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Courier New', monospace
ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: 9 clause gates · 4 probation tiers · 80% floor in cents · 5 issue codes
